data: s1/synthetic.py synthetic_pick_detour_v2, 300 episodes (seed 0), all successful. One active arm per episode (148 left, 152 right); the other arm idles at its rest pose. Two identical-looking fragments 14 cm apart on the active side; only the request fragment_pose says which one to pick (153 / 147). pick 0-1.4 s, place 1.4-3.4 s (carry past a 4 cm radius disc obstacle on the straight line, detour side +-1 with p = 1/2: 142 / 158, latent, privileged; release 2.9-3.2 s), retreat 3.4-4.6 s. Three 32x32 views (agent view missing in 65 episodes, labelled source umi); TCP 30 Hz; cameras 15 Hz, receive latency 20-50 ms, about 5% of frames dropped; commanded streams stamped at the reach time. Split by initial condition (one per episode here): 240/30/30 episodes, 10560/1320/1320 windows; no window dropped for gaps or stale state (counters absent = 0).
evaluation: Held-out test episodes, 8 DDIM-16 samples per window (generator seed 99), raw predictions before S1 forces the hold. Phases: pick_first (pick start), place_first (carry about to start, mode unobservable), place_mid (0.7 s later, mode visible), place_late (1.6 s, future past the segment end), arms (all evaluated windows: max xy excursion of the requested and the other arm). Mode, chosen fragment and obstacle come from privileged.npz for evaluation only.
criteria: v3, s1/smoke.py docstring (C1-C10), written before either code_v4 run and not changed after the results

exploratory_diagnosis.status: post hoc, after the v3 verdict of the maxwell run; changes no verdict, criterion or code
exploratory_diagnosis.question: Do C3 and C10 fail because of the trained network or because of the deterministic DDIM-16 sampler?
exploratory_diagnosis.method: reports/s1_smoke/diagnose_sampler.py re-evaluates the saved EMA checkpoint of the maxwell run on the same test windows with the same evaluation code and deterministic kernels; only the sampler changes. The ddim_16 variant reproduces metrics.json exactly (max abs diff 0.0). A first pass without deterministic kernels moved rates by up to 1/30 episodes and distances by up to 0.14 mm.
exploratory_diagnosis.finding: The same network sampled with DDPM-100 meets both failed thresholds (place_first hits 0.096, inactive-arm median 3.4 mm) but takes 487 ms per sample. At the deployed cost of 16 network calls, DDIM with eta = 1 gives 0.167 hits (still above 0.15) and 4.8 mm. Deterministic DDIM-100 gives 0.171 and 13.1 mm, so the gap comes mostly from the deterministic sampler, not from too few steps. Without x0 clipping DDIM-16 diverges (tens of metres).
exploratory_diagnosis.not_tested: a verdict run with eta = 1 or with longer training (val loss still fell 5% over the last 1000 of 8000 steps); both need criteria declared before the run.

notes: Verdict of the maxwell reference run: FAIL. C3 fails on the obstacle hit rate alone (0.217 > 0.15; left fraction 0.60, both modes in 28/30 episodes, final error 1.7 cm all pass). C10 fails on the inactive arm (median raw excursion 2.0 cm > 1 cm, p90 5.1 cm; active arm 19.7 cm). C1, C2, C4-C9 pass.

C10 measures the network output only. On the deployment path S1 overwrites the inactive arm with an exact hold at its last commanded width; all 64 deployment-path chunks were contract-valid and executable (C6).
The arm and fragment conditioning works: pick_first goes to the requested fragment in 98.3% of samples (regression 96.7%), and the requested arm moves about 10 times as far as the other one.
Regression baseline: place_first hits 0.80 with no episode showing both modes and a median clearance of -2.5 cm (through the obstacle), so C4 passes by a wide margin (0.80 >= 0.217 + 0.15).

Compared with the superseded synthetic_detour_v1 runs (diffusion hits 0.017, clearance 7.4 cm), v2 adds the arm choice, two fragments and three skills with the same 8000 training steps, and its demonstrations keep a smaller clearance (median 5.9 cm versus 7.9 cm).

DDIM-16 latency on the shared maxwell GPU: median 80.7 ms, p90 101.3 ms (budget 100 ms for the median). Deployment-path live_sample -> ActionChunk: median 64.9 ms, max 108.7 ms, under the 250 ms valid_until.
Torch job 20226851 (same v4 bundle, L40S) ran after the v4 section was written (06:02-06:14) and fails C3 and C10 with the same values; it is listed under comparison_runs, not as a verdict.
limitations: Synthetic data only: no Isaac, UMI or robot episodes exist yet, so nothing here measures skull assembly ability.
Images are 32x32 top-down rasters; the real three-view resolution, crops and a pretrained encoder are untested.
Training preloads the whole split onto the GPU; real datasets need a streaming loader.
The maxwell GPU was shared with other users during the run, so its latency numbers include contention.
All synthetic episodes succeed and carry no oracle inputs or stream gaps; the success filter, oracle refusal and gap dropping are exercised only by the unit tests.
Mode-coverage metrics depend on privileged ground truth and the synthetic generator; they are a sanity check of the method, not a benchmark.

superseded_context.data: s1/synthetic.py synthetic_detour_v1, 300 episodes (seed 0), split 240/30/30 episodes (5040/630/630 windows) by episode; left hand carries part_0 past a disc obstacle on the straight line, passing left or right with p=1/2 (latent, privileged); right hand inactive; 3 views 32x32 (agent view missing in 57 of 300 episodes, labelled source umi); TCP 30 Hz, cameras 15 Hz with jitter and 5% drops
superseded_context.evaluation: first place-segment window of each held-out episode (hand still at rest, mode unobservable), 8 DDIM-16 samples per episode; obstacle/target/mode ground truth read from privileged.npz for evaluation only
superseded_context.criteria: s1/smoke.py docstring: C1 pytest counts, C2 checkpoint reload, C3 diffusion modes/hits/final error, C4 regression averages modes, C5 DDIM-16 latency <= 100 ms; C6 (end-to-end live_sample -> ActionChunk) added before the final run only
notes: C4 passed with a narrow margin in both runs (regression 0.333 vs required 0.317). The deterministic regression baseline does not always average the modes: in 20 of 30 held-out episodes it commits to one side (sides split 45/55), and in 10 it drives through the obstacle. Its median closest approach is 2.7 cm outside the obstacle versus 7.4 cm for diffusion and 7.9 cm for the demonstrations.
Only 23.8% of the 6,300 training windows are mode-ambiguous (observation before the reach starts); the rest reveal the mode through the hand motion history.

Batch-1 latency budget: one 10 Hz policy step is 100 ms; DDIM-16 measured 55-76 ms on L40S nodes and 262 ms on a loaded maxwell CPU (8 threads), so CPU-only deployment would need fewer DDIM steps or a smaller model.

Runs 20219996 (gl038, S1 code faf31f75) and 20221507 (gl063, S1 code 9498adb9) produced bitwise-identical train and validation loss logs, final losses and evaluation metrics for both policies (max abs difference 0.0). The second revision refactored how windows are assembled (shared encode_observation/live_sample) and added the inference check and runtime wrapper, so this also shows the refactor did not change the training data. Checkpoint files differ only because their metadata differs.

Batch-1 latency differed between nodes: DDIM-16 median 55.1 ms on gl038 and 75.7 ms on gl063 (both under the 100 ms criterion); end-to-end live_sample -> ActionChunk median 76.1 ms, max 78.9 ms on gl063, against a 250 ms valid_until.
limitations: Synthetic data only: no Isaac, UMI or robot episodes exist yet, so nothing here measures skull assembly ability.
Images are 32x32 top-down rasters; the real three-view resolution, crops and a pretrained encoder are untested (encoder weights=None).
Training preloads the whole split onto the GPU; real datasets need a streaming loader.
Reproducibility was checked only on L40S nodes with driver 610.43.02 (two runs, two nodes); other GPU models, drivers or batch sizes are untested.
Episode schema carries no joint diagnostics or action issue times yet (INTERFACES lists both).
Mode-coverage metrics depend on privileged ground truth and the synthetic generator; they are a sanity check of the method, not a benchmark.
